chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) validated the testimony of women along with the oath of the claimant in a debt, when he swears by Allah that his right is indeed due.
ai.seo_question: How is a debt proven in Shia jurisprudence using women's testimony and an oath?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential mechanism of *qasam* (oath) complementing witness testimony (*shahada*) in debt disputes, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding evidentiary standards. It highlights the Prophet’s validation of combining female witnesses with the claimant’s oath, offering a practical legal solution when full male testimony is unavailable. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia evidence law in commercial transactions while maintaining strict adherence to divine authority.
